answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake before it may vote on a task, then slash that stake if its work fails a randomly selected, independently checked audit. One operator can still create many agents, but every extra identity ties up capital, and coordinated low-quality submissions risk losing it; passing audits does not prove unique humans, yet makes mass Sybils costly. A summit may set the stake, an oasis pool may fund audits, and a quill may record penalties.
